_about: The break queue. Vendor A and Vendor B values are MOCKED for the demo; every source page is retrieved by Exa. Queries, subjects and dates are fixed text so each request body is identical every run and its saved run keeps matching. live_path true = on the demo path, in demo_order.

rows.break_summary: 1-for-10 reverse split, effective Sep 29 2026. Vendor B has no new CUSIP.
rows.subject: OneMedNet Corp (Nasdaq: ONMD)
rows.issuer_query: Press release from OneMedNet Corp (Nasdaq: ONMD) announcing a reverse stock split, with the ratio, the effective date and time, the first day of split-adjusted trading, and the new CUSIP
rows.market_query: Nasdaq Equity Corporate Actions Alert for OneMedNet Corp (ONMD) reverse stock split and CUSIP change, with the effective date

presenter.hypothesis: Vendor B has not picked up OneMedNet's new CUSIP. If the split is real, the issuer's release and the Nasdaq alert should both print the same new CUSIP.
presenter.action: One Exa search per channel, run at the same time: the press-release wires, and nasdaqtrader.com. Then plain code, not a model, compares the fields.
presenter.expected: Both channels find it: 1-for-10, effective Sep 29. The issuer prints the CUSIP as 68270C 202 with a space and Nasdaq prints 68270C202. Code strips the space, so the row is corroborated by two independent sources and Vendor A is right.
presenter.if_different: If one channel comes back empty, I open Show request to confirm the domain list, then open the identity guard panel to see whether the right page was found but dropped.

rows.break_summary: 1-for-25 reverse split. Vendors disagree on the effective date by one day; both show CUSIP 20678X700.
rows.subject: CDT Equity Inc. (Nasdaq: CDT)
rows.issuer_query: Press release from CDT Equity Inc. (Nasdaq: CDT) announcing a reverse stock split, with the split ratio, the effective date and time, the first day of split-adjusted trading, and the new CUSIP
rows.market_query: Nasdaq Equity Corporate Actions Alert for CDT Equity Inc. (CDT) announcing a reverse stock split and a CUSIP change, with the effective date

presenter.hypothesis: The vendors are one day apart. My guess is they read the same event but mean different dates: the legal effective time versus the first day it trades on the new terms.
presenter.action: The same pair of searches. Code checks every page for CDT Equity by exchange-prefixed ticker, CUSIP or legal name, because CDT on its own is also Central Daylight Time.
presenter.expected: The issuer release says effective September 28 at 5:00 pm Eastern, first split-adjusted trading September 29. Live (checked 2026-10-02): Nasdaq alert 2026-683 now agrees on 1-for-25, September 29 and CUSIP 20678X700, so the label is corroborated by two independent sources, with a note that the two dates mean different things. Vendor A loaded the legal date, Vendor B the trading date. The saved run from September 29 predates the alert, so in Saved runs only mode the label is single source, issuer only.
presenter.if_different: If the market channel does find alert 683, I check that its date is the first trading day, Sep 29. If the issuer page is dropped, I open the identity guard panel to see which rule rejected it.

rows.issuer_display: Bank of America Floating Rate Senior Notes due September 2027
rows.break_summary: Redemption. Vendor A shows the notes redeemed on Sep 15 2026; Vendor B still shows them outstanding.
rows.subject: Bank of America Floating Rate Senior Notes due September 2027, CUSIP 06051GLX5
rows.issuer_query: Press release from Bank of America announcing the redemption of its Floating Rate Senior Notes due September 2027, CUSIP 06051GLX5, with the redemption date and redemption price
rows.market_query: Bank of America SEC filing about the redemption of Floating Rate Senior Notes due September 2027, CUSIP 06051GLX5

presenter.hypothesis: Vendor B still shows the floating-rate notes as outstanding. If Bank of America redeemed them, its own release names this CUSIP and the redemption date.
presenter.action: The issuer channel adds Bank of America's newsroom to the wires. The market channel is sec.gov. For a bond, code identifies the security by issuer plus CUSIP, or coupon plus maturity when no CUSIP is printed.
presenter.expected: The Sep 4 release: redeemed on Sep 15 at 100 percent plus accrued interest. sec.gov finds nothing relevant. Single source, issuer only. The release covers two series, and a Canadian-dollar release uses the same due September 2027 wording, so code keeps only pages that print this CUSIP.
presenter.if_different: If sec.gov returns a filing, I check it is Bank of America's and names 06051GLX5. An 8-K exhibit is usually the same release filed again, so that would be same-issuer confirmation, not an independent source.

rows.issuer_display: Cheetah Net Supply Chain Service Inc.
rows.break_summary: Reverse split per Nasdaq alert 2026-677. Vendor A has a new CUSIP; Vendor B has none.
rows.subject: Cheetah Net Supply Chain Service Inc. (Nasdaq: CTNT)
rows.issuer_query: Press release from Cheetah Net Supply Chain Service Inc. (Nasdaq: CTNT) announcing a reverse stock split, with the split ratio, the effective date, and the new CUSIP
rows.market_query: Nasdaq Equity Corporate Actions Alert for Cheetah Net Supply Chain Service Inc. (CTNT) announcing a reverse stock split and a CUSIP change, with the effective date

presenter.hypothesis: Vendor B has no new CUSIP for Cheetah Net. The Nasdaq alert should settle it.
presenter.action: The same two searches. If the alert page Exa has stored is a placeholder, code tries one live re-fetch of that exact URL through /contents, forcing a fresh crawl.
presenter.expected: No reverse-split release on the wires. Exa's stored copy of alert 2026-677 reads Page Not Available, so code sends one live re-fetch. Both outcomes were seen on Sep 29: at 09:19 ET the re-fetch said success but returned an empty page, which code treats as a failure (not confirmed, route to analyst); at 09:40 ET it returned the real alert, 1-for-150, effective Monday Sep 28, CUSIP 16307X400 (stale source repaired, one source, analyst confirms).
presenter.if_different: If the re-fetch returns real text, I check that it names Cheetah Net before trusting it, and it still goes to the analyst as one repaired source, never as corroborated. If it comes back empty, I name it as a coverage gap: which alerts are indexed, and what the fix on Exa's side would be.
